sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F177].
The window bottomed at $94.5 billion in FY2020, then reached $235.7 billion by FY2022, a 51.5% jump in that year alone [F5][F7][D232].
That FY2022 surge came from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins, which the filing credits for the $28.0 billion rise in pre-tax income [P57].
Revenue then fell in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, to $184.4 billion, a 7.9% three-year CAGR [F8][F9][F10][D626].
The FY2025 decline was mainly lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes and natural gas prices [P17].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue and subtracted 3.9pp from growth as it fell 5.3% [D402][D403][D404].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, at 11.6% of revenue and up 16.5%, adding 1.5pp [D418][D419][D420].
The U.S. upstream segment grew 34.0% and added 2.5pp, helped by the Hess acquisition and Permian and Gulf of America production [D553][D554][P24].
Profit grew slower than revenue: net income fell 30.5% against a 4.6% revenue decline, and operating costs fell only 3.4% [D359][D358][D373].
Diluted EPS fell 31.8% while net income fell 30.5%, as the diluted share count rose 2.1% [D361][D359][D374].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025, below the 7.9% window median and far under the 15.1% FY2022 high [F30][D613][D612].
Cost of revenue fell to 57.2% of revenue from 58.8%, a 1.6pp tailwind, while SG&A rose 0.3pp to 2.7% [D338][D296][D340][D298].
SG&A rose because of the Hess acquisition and higher professional service costs, partly offset by lower severance accruals [P13].
Depreciation, depletion and amortization rose to 10.7% of revenue from 8.5% on higher production and higher rates [D341][D299][P12].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5%, widening the gap between pre-tax and net margin [D345][D303].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income, above the 1.97x window median [F60][F20][D346][D644].
The FY2025 increase was mainly higher cash distributions from TCO and contributions from legacy Hess assets, partly offset by lower commodity prices [P6].
Free cash flow was $16.6 billion, an 8.8% margin against a 8.9% median, with capex at 9.2% of revenue and 0.86x D&A [F80][D343][D616][D342][D348].
Free cash flow covered net income 1.35x, above the 1.10x median [D347][D622].
Cash and investments were $7.3 billion at FY2025, down 11.8%, against $2.3 billion of current debt and $977 million of short-term borrowings [D349][D375][X177][X187].
Total assets jumped 26.1% to $324.0 billion and equity 22.4% to $186.5 billion, lifting the current ratio to 1.15x against a 1.17x median [D365][F110][D367][F176][F160][D625].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow, funded partly by $11.4 billion of debt issued [D353][D354][X157].
The diluted share count still rose 2.1% in FY2025 despite $12.1 billion of repurchases [D374][X132].
Revenue has fallen for three straight years, from $196.9 billion in FY2023 to $184.4 billion in FY2025 [R1][F8][F10].
Payouts exceeded free cash flow in each of those years, at 132.8%, 179.7% and 149.7% [R4][D270][D312][D354].
The metrics table uses recast revenue for FY2018 through FY2025, so growth rates mixing recast and first-reported years compare two presentations [R3][F10][X10].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021, so total debt and net cash after that omit it and no leverage conclusion should rest on them [R12][X193].
Watch whether net margin recovers toward the 7.9% median from 6.7%, or falls toward the -5.9% FY2020 low, in the FY2026 10-K [D613][F30][D611].
Watch free cash flow against the $24.8 billion payout: a margin below the 8.9% median would keep buybacks and dividends above free cash flow [D616][D353].
Watch capex against the $18-19 billion 2026 guidance, versus $17.3 billion in FY2025, for pressure on the 8.8% free-cash-flow margin [P4][F70][D343].
